summary.en: Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan warned Beijing could easily win a conflict with the Philippines, prompting PCG Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela to call the remark a direct threat. The Philippines launched a five-day maritime defence drill along the eastern Mindanao coast and the Philippines and the United States carried out their 16th bilateral maritime exercise in the West Philippine Sea. Japan began providing modernization support to the Philippine Coast Guard and the PCG opened an upgraded station on Pag-asa Island. Chinese naval assets were monitored near Scarborough Shoal, and the Philippines and Japan held an anti-piracy drill in Manila Bay. 176 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Kinesisk ambassadør Jing Quan advarte at Beijing lett kunne vinne en konflikt med Filippinene, noe som fikk PCG-rear Admiral Jay Tarriela til å kalle bemerkningen en direkte trussel. Filippinene igangsatte en fem-dagers maritimt forsvarsøvelse langs den østlige kysten av Mindanao, og Filippinene og USA gjennomførte sin 16. bilaterale maritime øvelse i Vestfilippinene. Japan begynte å gi moderniseringsstøtte til Filippinenes kystvakt, og PCG åpnet en oppgradert stasjon på Pag-asa-øya. Kinesiske marineenheter ble overvåket nær Scarborough-revet, og Filippinene og Japan holdt en anti-piratøvelse i Manila-bukta. 176 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Moro conflict
background.extract: The Moro conflict was an insurgency in the Mindanao region in southern Philippines which involved multiple armed groups. A decades-long peace process has resulted in peace deals between the Philippine government and two major armed groups, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), but other smaller armed groups continue to exist. In 2017, the peace council settled around 138 clan conflicts.
